reason: Conversation 2 correctly identified the Miele T1 layout from the start: a removable foam plinth filter behind the bottom flap with fixed heat exchanger fins behind it to be vacuumed gently without bending, matched the 'clean airways' message, gave a sensible escalation threshold and correctly confirmed just over 2 hours is normal with no part needed. Conversation 1 reached the right area but conflated the plinth filter with the heat exchanger, repeatedly told the owner to pull the finned unit out and rinse it under a tap (not possible or advisable on a T1 heat pump), repeated itself almost verbatim, then abruptly refused to give removal instructions citing 'sharp edges', leaving the owner confused and padding the exchange with unneeded sensor-strip and vinegar advice. Conversation 1 did explicitly say to switch off and unplug first, which Conversation 2 omitted, but that minor safety plus is outweighed by Conversation 1's inaccurate, inefficient guidance.
